messages.text: FIA confirms Mercedes granted engine upgrades despite Red Bull complaints

metadata.summary: The FIA has confirmed that Mercedes have been granted the opportunity to make upgrades to their engine despite protestations from rival teams.
metadata.content: ADUO: FIA confirm Mercedes granted F1 engine upgrades despite complaints from rivals over test findings | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content ADUO: FIA confirm Mercedes granted F1 engine upgrades despite complaints from rivals over test findings The FIA has confirmed findings from the first two periods of performance review; Red Bull were adjudged to have the strongest engine in the first period, giving the other manufacturers upgrades; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6 Wednesday 26 August 2026 17:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen said in June that Red Bull were shocked by the FIA's findings in the first ADUO review period. The FIA has confirmed that Mercedes have been granted the opportunity to make upgrades to their engine despite protestations from rival teams. Following the introduction of all-new engines for the 2026 season, Formula 1's governing body implemented an Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) system, designed to allow manufacturers to catch up to the performance of the leading power unit during the rules cycle. It was revealed in June after the first round of performance assessment, which included the first five rounds of the season, that the FIA had adjudged Red Bull to have the strongest engine and had granted upgrades to Mercedes, Ferrari, Audi and Honda. messages.text: Williams sisters given wild card for US Open women's doubles

metadata.summary: Serena and Venus Williams will play together in the 2026 US Open women's doubles after being given a wild card to enter the tournament.
metadata.content: Serena and Venus Williams given wild card to compete in 2026 US Open women's doubles tournament | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Serena and Venus Williams given wild card to compete in 2026 US Open women's doubles tournament Serena and Venus Williams to play doubles together at a Grand Slam for the first time since the 2022 US Open; Serena played in mixed doubles alongside Carlos Alcaraz on Tuesday; watch the 2026 US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app Wednesday 26 August 2026 16:13, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Serena and Venus Williams against Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns from the Cincinnati Open Serena and Venus Williams will play together in the 2026 US Open women's doubles after being given a wild card to enter the tournament. The sisters played competitively together for the first time since the 2022 US Open at the Cincinnati Open earlier this month, and will now return to Grand Slam action at the scene of their last major outing as a pair. Serena made a sensational return to tennis during the grass-court season after almost four years out of the professional game, but the 44-year-old suffered a knee injury during a first-round singles loss at Wimbledon which led to her and Venus withdrawing from the doubles at the All England Club. messages.text: Solheim Cup captain Nordqvist announces shock mid-season retirement

metadata.summary: Solheim Cup captain Anna Nordqvist has announced via social media that she will retire from playing professional golf after this week's FM Championship, live on Sky Sports.
metadata.content: Anna Nordqvist: Team Europe's Solheim Cup captain announces shock mid-season retirement from playing professional golf | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Anna Nordqvist: Team Europe's Solheim Cup captain announces shock mid-season retirement from playing professional golf Three-time major winner and nine-time Solheim Cup player Anna Nordqvist will retire from playing professional golf at the FM Championship, ending her 18-year professional career; Nordqvist will captain Team Europe at the Solheim Cup from September 11-13, live on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Wednesday 26 August 2026 14:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anna Nordqvist announced her retirement from playing professional golf with an emotional video posted on her Instagram page Solheim Cup captain Anna Nordqvist has announced via social media that she will retire from playing professional golf after this week's FM Championship, live on Sky Sports . The three-time major winner will captain Team Europe at Bernardus Golf from September 11-13, having featured in each of the previous nine Solheim Cups as a player and been part of five winning teams. Nordqvist has been a playing vice-captain in the last two contests but quickly ruled herself out of juggling captaincy with playing against Team USA in the Netherlands, despite still regularly featuring on the LPGA Tour and impressing in the majors.
